**Grant Application: Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC)**

Glocks and Fried Chicken (GAFC), a minority-owned social enterprise, requests $25,000 from the Sacramento Stockton Blvd Grant to expand vital gun safety education within Sacramento's communities of color.

Communities of color disproportionately bear the brunt of gun violence and accidental shootings. Traditional safety education often fails to engage, leaving a critical gap in preventative knowledge and resources for our youth and families along Stockton Blvd. GAFC innovatively fills this gap through culturally resonant programs. These include "Gloxsie 21," an engaging cartoon IP for youth; empowering AI education that subtly integrates safety principles; and practical community workshops, often delivered in partnership with the trusted Church of Legacy, offering hands-on skills and awareness.

This funding will significantly enhance gun safety awareness and responsible firearm practices among hundreds of Sacramento residents. We project a measurable reduction in preventable gun-related incidents, fostering safer homes and stronger communities along Stockton Blvd. Our work empowers individuals, builds resilience, and saves lives.

As a minority-owned organization, GAFC brings authentic understanding and a trusted voice directly into the communities most impacted. Our unique blend of pop culture, technology, and grassroots engagement, alongside our strong Church of Legacy partnership, positions us perfectly to deliver impactful, sustainable change and foster a safer future.
